Where does a message enter?

A new order enters the service through one HTTP route. The table names this entry point and links to its flow.

order.mmd:1 flowchart
KindNameFlow
httpPOST /ordersorder

What happens to a new order?

The controller takes the order body and checks the total. A valid order is charged, saved and sent to Kafka.

order.mmd:1 flowchart

Which events move through the order service?

The service has three events. Each one goes to the orders stream. OrderPlaced carries the main flow of a new order.

In the table, E means that the component emits the event. C means that it consumes the event. (C) means that it receives the event and ignores it. A mark that is a link opens the flow of the order. An empty cell means no line in the map.

EventOrderControllerPaymentHandlerOrderProjection
OrderPlacedECC
OrderPaidE(C)
OrderRejectedEC
order.mmd:1 flowchart
OrderPlaced

The payload is the order body. The stream is orders. OrderController emits the event for a valid order. PaymentHandler and OrderProjection consume it.

order.mmd:1 flowchart
OrderPaid

The payload is the payment id. The stream is orders. PaymentHandler emits the event after a charge. OrderProjection receives it and ignores it.

order.mmd:1 flowchart
OrderRejected

The payload is the reason. The stream is orders. OrderController emits the event for an order over the limit. OrderProjection consumes it.
